stage.title: Generation stage
stage.body: Choose which part of the workflow to run. Preview selection and refinement are separate submissions.

preview.title: Seed previews
preview.body: Generate 1–3 alternatives at the preview size. Watch them, select one, then render its saved latent with separate refinement settings.

single.title: Single pass
single.body: Generate one video directly at the draft resolution. There is no separate selected-preview refinement step.

continuation.title: Continue a video
continuation.body: Generate a new segment guided by the end of the selected source section. Overlap frames join that segment to the source.

dialogue.title: Dialogue / audio previews
dialogue.body: Generate voice/audio alternatives. The dialogue builder inserts your lines into the visible prompt. Downloadable FLAC is the primary result.

final.title: Saved latent refinement
final.body: Use the selected preview’s saved result and conditioning. The prompt, base model, encoder, frames and original references stay tied to that preview.

model.title: H3 model
model.body: The main video/audio generator. Seed Hunter uses Ref2VA H3 weights. A different checkpoint or quantization can change appearance, memory use and which LoRAs work.

encoder.title: Text encoder
encoder.body: Converts the prompt and supported reference context into conditioning for H3. This is separate from the optional chat model used by Enhance prompt. NVFP4 encoder weights need a compatible Blackwell GPU.

video_vae.title: Video VAE
video_vae.body: Encodes input pictures/video into latents and decodes generated latents into frames. Use an H3-compatible VAE. This choice affects memory, decoding performance and reconstruction.

audio_vae.title: Audio VAE
audio_vae.body: Encodes reference audio and decodes generated audio. It must be compatible with H3; it uses the VAE GPU selection.

latent_upscaler.title: Latent upscaler
latent_upscaler.body: The learned model that enlarges the selected preview’s compressed video before refinement. It does not replace the video VAE or add video duration.

gpu.title: Model / encoder GPU
gpu.body: Runs H3 denoising and the Qwen text encoder. NVFP4 components require a compatible Blackwell GPU. Selecting a VAE GPU separately does not split H3’s denoising across both cards.

vae_gpu.title: VAE GPU
vae_gpu.body: Runs video/audio encoding and decoding. A second GPU can keep those workloads off the main GPU; it does not share the denoising work. Blank uses the model GPU.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.body: Describe the intended scene, action, speech and sound. Name attached references as <Picture 1>, <Video 1> and <Audio 1> in their listed order. References guide generation; they do not guarantee an exact copy.

prompt_enhancement.title: Enhance prompt
prompt_enhancement.body: Ask the selected language model to rewrite this visible draft for H3. Review the result before queueing. Enhancement is a separate action and does not start video generation.

enhancement_model.title: Enhancement model
enhancement_model.body: The running chat/vision model that rewrites the prompt. It is not H3’s text encoder. Image context requires a vision-capable endpoint; check the context note for the inputs being sent.

dialogue_text.title: Line of dialogue
dialogue_text.body: The words inserted at {{dialogue}} when you choose Build visible prompt. They are not sent until that resulting prompt is used for a job.

dialogue_tone.title: Tone and delivery
dialogue_tone.body: Delivery directions inserted at {{tone}}, such as calm, hurried or whispered. The model still interprets these instructions rather than playing a fixed recording.

dialogue_template.title: Editable prompt template
dialogue_template.body: Controls the visible dialogue prompt. {{dialogue}} and {{tone}} are replaced by the two fields above when you build it; you can edit the resulting prompt afterward.

width.title: Preview width
width.body: Horizontal pixels generated for this stage, in multiples of 32. More pixels increase work and memory. Saved-preview refinement chooses its own final width.

height.title: Preview height
height.body: Vertical pixels generated for this stage, in multiples of 32. Width and height together determine the aspect ratio and pixel count.

frames.title: Frames at 24 fps
frames.body: Sampling length: frames ÷ 24 gives seconds. H3 uses counts of 5 + 17×n. In Hunter Preview mode this controls each short candidate, independently of the final output length. In single-pass and Scout batches, automatic length selects a supported count per clip. This is independent of sampling steps.

steps.title: Sampling steps
steps.body: How many denoising updates refine the entire clip. 8 steps means 8 passes through noise levels, not 8 frames or seconds. More steps usually take longer; a turbo LoRA may be trained for a small specific count.

seed.title: Base seed
seed.body: Controls the initial random noise. Preview alternatives use this seed, seed + 1000 and seed + 2000. Keeping seed and all settings fixed helps comparisons; device/runtime changes can still change results.

preview_count.title: Preview count
preview_count.body: Generate 1, 2 or 3 seed alternatives within each preview job. They run sequentially. Each batch input gets this many alternatives; single pass, continuation and refinement use one.

scout_count.title: Scout seed count
scout_count.body: Try 1–32 consecutive seeds, starting at the base seed and increasing by 1. Each runs through the Scout step before its preview is shown. More seeds add sampling work; interactive mode also retains their partial latents until you choose one.

scout_step.title: Scout stopping step
scout_step.body: How many steps of the full sampling schedule to run for each seed before comparing previews. In interactive or preview-only mode, it must be before the last sampling step. A later stopping point gives more developed previews at greater cost. Interactive mode continues the selected seed’s exact partial latent through the remaining steps.

scout_mode.title: Scout mode
scout_mode.body: Choose whether to compare seeds and continue a selection, stop at partial previews, or generate one seed directly.

interactive.title: Choose and continue
interactive.body: Preview each seed, then wait for your selection. The same job resumes the chosen seed’s saved partial latent through the rest of the full schedule.

scout.title: Scout previews only
scout.body: Generate the partial previews and stop without waiting for a selection. The job’s output is the first seed’s partial result; it has not completed the full sampling schedule.

final.title: Single full pass
final.body: Run the full schedule once with the current base seed. This skips the seed search and selection wait and starts a new pass; it does not resume a partial latent from an earlier job.

scout_timeout.title: Selection timeout
scout_timeout.body: Seconds to wait for your choice in interactive mode. 0 waits until you select a seed or cancel the job. A positive timeout stops the job with an error when it expires; it never chooses a seed automatically.

scout_preview_mode.title: Scout preview display
scout_preview_mode.body: How to display the partially sampled video for each seed. These previews help compare candidates before completing the schedule.

vae.title: VAE decode
vae.body: Decode previews with the video VAE for a more representative image. This adds decoding work and memory use.

latent2rgb.title: Fast latent colors
latent2rgb.body: Convert latent values directly into rough color previews. This avoids a VAE preview decode, but colors and detail are less representative of the completed video.

preview_megapixels.title: Preview megapixels
preview_megapixels.body: A size helper: Apply preview size converts this pixel-area target and aspect ratio into width/height rounded to 32. It changes the draft only when applied. Larger sizes need more memory.

preview_aspect.title: Preview aspect ratio
preview_aspect.body: The width:height proportion used by Apply preview size. 9:16 is portrait; 16:9 is landscape. It does not crop or trim an attached source file.

preview_seconds.title: Preview seconds
preview_seconds.body: Changing this value immediately sets each candidate's duration to the next supported H3 frame count at 24 fps. For example, 4 seconds selects 107 frames, about 4.46 seconds. Three candidates each use this length. Automatic final-length matching does not lengthen the previews.

final_frames.title: Final output length
final_frames.body: The final video's frame count at 24 fps, separate from the short preview duration. Automatic matching chooses a supported count covering the primary reference video or chosen section. If this differs from the preview, the final job generates a full-length candidate using the selected seed and saved preview settings before spatial upscale and refinement. The result can differ from the short audition. Matching lengths reuse its exact saved latent.

sampler.title: Sampler
sampler.body: The numerical method that turns each model prediction into the next denoising update. It works with the scheduler; no sampler is always fastest or best.

euler.title: Euler
euler.body: A first-order update using the current prediction. A straightforward baseline with no history-based correction. These settings use one model evaluation per scheduled update.

res_multistep.title: RES multistep
res_multistep.body: Uses the current and previous denoising predictions for a second-order correction after its initial Euler step. Reuses history rather than adding a second model evaluation each step.

er_sde.title: ER-SDE
er_sde.body: A stochastic solver using prediction history for higher-order corrections as steps progress. It can inject seeded noise during sampling. The supplied Seed Hunter workflow uses this for preview and refinement.

scheduler.title: Scheduler
scheduler.body: Chooses the sequence of noise levels visited during the steps. It does not control video timing, job order or how many frames are generated.

simple.title: Simple
simple.body: Selects evenly spaced entries from the model’s stored noise-level table, then ends at zero. The word “simple” is a schedule name, not a lower-quality mode.

normal.title: Normal
normal.body: Spaces points evenly along the model’s timestep range, converts them to noise levels, and ends at zero. It can be close to Simple for some models, but endpoint spacing differs.

beta.title: Beta
beta.body: Uses a beta-distribution spacing that places more points near the ends of the timestep range than the middle. This is the supplied Seed Hunter preview default.

linear_quadratic.title: Linear quadratic
linear_quadratic.body: Combines an initially linear noise-level curve with a quadratic segment, ending at zero. Its spacing differs from the model-table schedules. The supplied workflow uses it for low-denoise refinement; that does not make it universally better.

reference_size.title: Reference picture sizing
reference_size.body: Controls how still-image references are resized before encoding. The reference tokens are used throughout sampling.

max.title: Maximum
max.body: Uses the reference pipeline’s larger image sizing (up to a 2048-pixel short edge in this runtime). Can preserve more source detail while adding substantial sampling work and memory.

match.title: Match output
match.body: Scales images down, preserving aspect ratio, to at most the output pixel area. This can reduce reference tokens and memory compared with Maximum.

shift_enabled.title: Override video/audio shifts
shift_enabled.body: Enable to apply the two shift values. When off, the checkpoint’s model sampling defaults are used.

shift_video.title: Video shift
shift_video.body: Reshapes the flow/noise-time mapping for video. Larger values bias the mapping toward higher noise at the same underlying timestep. It is not a frame offset, duration setting or synchronization adjustment.

shift_audio.title: Audio shift
shift_audio.body: Reshapes audio’s flow/noise-time mapping relative to video. It is not a delay in seconds and does not shift the soundtrack on the timeline. Use values appropriate for the checkpoint/LoRA.

first_frame_guide.title: First-frame guide
first_frame_guide.body: Condition the beginning on an image. The dedicated first-frame attachment takes priority; otherwise Picture 1 is used. This is an explicit boundary guide rather than an ordinary reference.

last_frame_guide.title: Last-frame guide
last_frame_guide.body: Condition the ending on an image. The dedicated last-frame attachment takes priority; otherwise Picture 2 is used. This does not change the requested duration.

force_audio.title: Preserve supplied Audio 1 in the latent
force_audio.body: Insert the first supplied audio latent and mask it from denoising. This aims to preserve that audio through generation; VAE reconstruction and final encoding are not a bit-for-bit copy of the original file.

output_fps.title: Output frame rate
output_fps.body: H3 generates at 24 fps. The 48 fps option interpolates additional frames with RIFE after generation; it does not double the clip’s duration.

48.title: 48 fps
48.body: Use RIFE to insert intermediate frames for smoother playback. Requires the installed RIFE model and adds processing time.

attention_backend.title: Attention backend
attention_backend.body: Selects the implementation used for dense attention. Hardware support, memory use and numerical behavior can differ.

comfy kitchen attention.title: Comfy Kitchen
comfy kitchen attention.body: Uses the installed accelerated attention implementation when supported.

pytorch.title: PyTorch
pytorch.body: Uses PyTorch attention. Useful as a compatibility alternative; it is not guaranteed to use less memory or run faster.

sparse_method.title: Sparse attention
sparse_method.body: Approximates parts of attention to reduce work for long sequences. It can change output and requires compatible runtime/GPU support. Off keeps dense attention.

none.title: Off
none.body: Use the selected dense attention backend.

sol_attn.title: Sol-Attn
sol_attn.body: Chooses important blocks with an adaptive threshold. This integration uses the runtime threshold default; Kept (%) does not control this method.

sla.title: SLA
sla.body: Keeps a fixed fraction of high-scoring blocks. Use settings and model/LoRA weights intended for this attention pattern.

vsa.title: VSA
vsa.body: Uses 3D video-cube attention and a learned coarse branch when present. Intended for compatible FastH3/VSA weights, not a general quality switch.

sparse_keep_percent.title: Sparse attention kept (%)
sparse_keep_percent.body: Fraction of attention blocks retained by SLA, or video cubes retained by VSA. Lower values approximate more work and can change fidelity. Sol-Attn uses its own adaptive threshold and ignores this field.

sparse_start.title: Sparse attention start
sparse_start.body: Fraction through the denoising schedule where sparse attention starts: 0.2 means after the first 20%. Earlier sampling stays dense. This is not a timestamp in the output video.

sparse_end.title: Sparse attention end
sparse_end.body: Fraction through the denoising schedule where sparse attention stops: 1 means through the end. Later sampling returns to dense. Must be at least the start value.

sparse_min_tokens.title: Sparse minimum tokens
sparse_min_tokens.body: Keep attention dense when the packed sequence has fewer tokens than this threshold. Sparse overhead can outweigh savings on small sequences; tokens here include video and conditioning.

sparse_extra_tokens.title: Sparse extra tokens
sparse_extra_tokens.body: Additional high-scoring tokens considered beyond selected blocks. More can move the approximation closer to dense attention at added cost. Zero disables; VSA ignores this option.

sparse_sink_conditioning.title: Sparse reference preservation
sparse_sink_conditioning.body: Controls special treatment of conditioning during sparse attention.

exact_kv_and_rows.title: Preserve reference keys and rows
exact_kv_and_rows.body: Keeps text/audio/reference context exact and uses dense attention for protected query rows. Adds work but avoids sparsifying those paths.

none.title: Off
none.body: Disable the extra exact-conditioning treatment. This does not remove references from the prompt.

ff_chunk_size.title: Feed-forward chunks
ff_chunk_size.body: Number of feed-forward chunks: 4 splits a large token sequence into 4 calls. 0 enables automatic bounded memory protection for INT8 layers; other weight formats keep their normal path. An explicit count overrides that protection. Splitting lowers peak activation memory with possible overhead; it does not split the video into jobs.

ff_chunk_threshold.title: Feed-forward chunk threshold
ff_chunk_threshold.body: With an explicit chunk count above 1, split feed-forward work only when the packed token count exceeds this value. Automatic INT8 protection uses its own memory bound. This is a token count, not pixels or frames.

low_vram_chunks.title: Attention chunks
low_vram_chunks.body: Split attention heads into this many groups to reduce peak temporary GPU memory. 0 disables the patch. More groups add overhead; this is separate from sparse attention and does not intentionally discard attention links.

denoise.title: Refinement denoise
denoise.body: How far back into noise the saved, upscaled preview starts before refinement. Lower values preserve more of the existing latent; higher values allow larger changes. 0 skips denoising; 1 uses the full noise range. This is not LoRA strength.

upscaler_chunking.title: Temporal chunking for latent upscale
upscaler_chunking.body: Process the learned latent upscale in overlapping time chunks to reduce memory spikes on longer clips. It changes how the upscale is computed, not the final duration or number of jobs.

upscaler_force_unload.title: Unload latent upscaler after use
upscaler_force_unload.body: Move the upscaler’s weights to CPU after enlarging the latent, freeing their GPU memory before H3 refinement. Keeping it loaded can avoid a reload when reused, at the cost of VRAM.

continuation_overlap.title: Overlap frames
continuation_overlap.body: Number of frames shared between the source ending and the generated continuation. This guides and blends the join. Choose fewer overlap frames than the generated segment’s length.

source_start_seconds.title: Continuation source start
source_start_seconds.body: Start of the source section used for continuation, in original-video seconds. The end of the selected section becomes the continuation guide.

source_end_seconds.title: Continuation source end
source_end_seconds.body: End of the source section used for continuation, in original-video seconds. Blank uses the source end. Must be after Source start.

audio_start_seconds.title: Audio reference start
audio_start_seconds.body: Start of the voice/audio section to read, in seconds. Used before audio conditioning; it does not delay generated audio on the output timeline.

audio_end_seconds.title: Audio reference end
audio_end_seconds.body: End of the voice/audio section to read, in seconds. Blank uses the file end, subject to workflow limits. Must be after Audio start.

reference_images.title: Reference pictures
reference_images.body: Up to 9 image references, numbered <Picture 1>, <Picture 2>, etc. Describe each role in the prompt. These guide appearance and context rather than becoming fixed output frames unless guide options are enabled.

reference_videos.title: Reference videos
reference_videos.body: Up to 3 video references. Each chosen section is 2–15 seconds; selected sections total at most 15 seconds. A longer file can supply a later section. Generation length can limit how much reference content is consumed.

reference_audio.title: Reference audio
reference_audio.body: Up to 3 audio references, numbered <Audio 1>, <Audio 2>, etc., for sound or voice context. Describe how to use them. Ordinary references are not guaranteed to be copied exactly.

source_video.title: Continuation source video
source_video.body: The video to extend. Source start/end choose the portion used; overlap frames guide the transition. This source has a different role from the optional reference videos.

first_frame.title: Dedicated first-frame image
first_frame.body: Used when the first-frame guide option is enabled. If absent, the guide uses Picture 1 from the reference list.

last_frame.title: Dedicated last-frame image
last_frame.body: Used when the last-frame guide option is enabled. If absent, the guide uses Picture 2 from the reference list.

reference_mods.title: Reference mod bundles
reference_mods.body: Load up to 8 compatible .safetensors reference-conditioning bundles. These are precomputed reference data, not LoRA weights. Each bundle has its own strength.

refmod_strength.title: Reference mod strength
refmod_strength.body: Scale this bundle’s reference contribution from 0 to 1. 0 disables its contribution; 1 uses its full stored strength.

loras.title: LoRA stack
loras.body: Adapters applied in listed order to the H3 model. Each has its own strength and compatibility requirements. Combining adapters can change the sampling settings needed. Refinement starts with the selected preview’s saved stack.

lora_strength.title: LoRA strength
lora_strength.body: Scale this adapter’s effect. 0 disables it; larger magnitude means a stronger positive or negative contribution. A custom slider can define a different range. This is not a probability or a guarantee that instructions will be obeyed.

batch_job.title: Batch job
batch_job.body: Queue independent jobs using one input per job or repeated copies of a draft. Each submission captures the current prompt/settings. Earlier jobs keep their saved settings while you prepare another batch.

batch_input.title: Batch input
batch_input.body: The input that changes between jobs. All other enabled references and settings are shared. Turn batch off to use several reference videos together in one job.

auto_video_length.title: Automatically match each video’s length
auto_video_length.body: In Hunter Preview mode, match the final output length to each primary reference video while keeping every preview at the chosen short duration. In single-pass and Scout batches, match the generation length itself. Long references use up to 15 seconds unless you choose a section. Continuation, image/audio batches and draft copies retain their chosen generation length.

reference_start.title: Reference section start
reference_start.body: Seconds from the beginning of the original file. Use the preview to find a scene, then choose its current time as the start. This does not change the original file.

reference_duration.title: Reference section length
reference_duration.body: Maximum section length, from 2 to 15 seconds. If the file ends sooner, the remaining usable section is used. Automatic batch timing needs no manual section unless you want a different part.

batch_copies.title: Number of copies
batch_copies.body: Queue this many independent copies of the draft, including shared inputs and seed. This does not automatically randomize seeds; change the seed when you want different starting noise.

refine_preview.title: Render selected preview
refine_preview.body: Create a separate job from the selected preview’s saved latent. Review final size, denoise, sampler and LoRAs before submitting. The original preview remains available for other refinements.

final_width.title: Final width
final_width.body: Width after learned latent upscale, in multiples of 32. It must be at least the preview width. Increasing both edges can multiply GPU memory needs even with only a few refinement steps.

final_height.title: Final height
final_height.body: Height after learned latent upscale, in multiples of 32. Keep the preview’s aspect ratio unless you intend to reshape it. Final dimensions are separate from the draft above.

final_steps.title: Refinement steps
final_steps.body: Denoising updates at the enlarged resolution. 2 steps still processes the whole high-resolution video twice; it does not mean two frames. Use a step count appropriate to the model and LoRAs.

final_seed.title: Refinement seed
final_seed.body: Noise seed for this refinement pass. It can differ from the selected preview seed. Changing it makes another refinement variation while retaining the saved preview and conditioning.

final_loras.title: Refinement LoRA stack
final_loras.body: Applies only to the new refinement job. It initially copies the selected preview’s saved adapters; changing it does not alter the preview or the main draft.

final_denoise.title: Refinement denoise
final_denoise.body: How far back into noise the saved, upscaled preview starts before refinement. Lower values preserve more of the existing latent; higher values allow larger changes. 0 skips denoising; 1 uses the full noise range. This is not LoRA strength.

final_sampler.title: Sampler
final_sampler.body: The numerical method that turns each model prediction into the next denoising update. It works with the scheduler; no sampler is always fastest or best.

euler.title: Euler
euler.body: A first-order update using the current prediction. A straightforward baseline with no history-based correction. These settings use one model evaluation per scheduled update.

res_multistep.title: RES multistep
res_multistep.body: Uses the current and previous denoising predictions for a second-order correction after its initial Euler step. Reuses history rather than adding a second model evaluation each step.

er_sde.title: ER-SDE
er_sde.body: A stochastic solver using prediction history for higher-order corrections as steps progress. It can inject seeded noise during sampling. The supplied Seed Hunter workflow uses this for preview and refinement.

final_scheduler.title: Scheduler
final_scheduler.body: Chooses the sequence of noise levels visited during the steps. It does not control video timing, job order or how many frames are generated.

simple.title: Simple
simple.body: Selects evenly spaced entries from the model’s stored noise-level table, then ends at zero. The word “simple” is a schedule name, not a lower-quality mode.

normal.title: Normal
normal.body: Spaces points evenly along the model’s timestep range, converts them to noise levels, and ends at zero. It can be close to Simple for some models, but endpoint spacing differs.

beta.title: Beta
beta.body: Uses a beta-distribution spacing that places more points near the ends of the timestep range than the middle. This is the supplied Seed Hunter preview default.

linear_quadratic.title: Linear quadratic
linear_quadratic.body: Combines an initially linear noise-level curve with a quadratic segment, ending at zero. Its spacing differs from the model-table schedules. The supplied workflow uses it for low-denoise refinement; that does not make it universally better.

final_latent_upscaler.title: Latent upscaler
final_latent_upscaler.body: The learned model that enlarges the selected preview’s compressed video before refinement. It does not replace the video VAE or add video duration.
